title: Module 1: The Birth of C++
description: Discover the origins of C++ and write your first program.
story_text:
# 📜 The Legend of Bjarne

Imagine it's 1979. A computer scientist named **Bjarne Stroustrup** is sitting at Bell Labs. He wants a language as fast as C but organized like Simula.

He creates 'C with Classes', which later becomes **C++**.

Your journey begins here. The first tradition of every programmer is to say Hello to the world.
quiz_data: [{"question": "Who created C++?", "options": ["Dennis Ritchie", "Bjarne Stroustrup", "Ada Lovelace", "Bill Gates"], "answer": 1}, {"question": "What is std::cout used for?", "options": ["Input", "Output", "Loops", "Math"], "answer": 1}, {"question": "What symbol ends a statement?", "options": [".", ",", ";", ":"], "answer": 2}]
hints: Statements must end with a semicolon ';'

title: Module 2: Variables (The Storage Boxes)
description: Learn how to store data using integers and strings.
story_text:
# 📦 storage Boxes

Computers need to store data. In C++, we use **variables**.

- `int`: Integers (1, 2, -5)
- `double`: Decimals (3.14, 0.5)
- `string`: Text ("Hello")

Unlike Python, C++ is statically typed. You cannot put a string into an integer box!
quiz_data: [{"question": "Which type holds whole numbers?", "options": ["float", "int", "string", "bool"], "answer": 1}, {"question": "How do you declare a variable?", "options": ["x = 10;", "int x = 10;", "var x = 10;", "let x = 10"], "answer": 1}]
hints: 'name' holds text, so it should be a std::string

title: Module 3: Input (cin)
description: Learn to take input from the user.
story_text:
# 📥 Listening to Users

`cout` talks to the user. `cin` listens.

Use `>>` arrows pointing INTO the variable.

```cpp
int x;
std::cin >> x;
```
quiz_data: [{"question": "Which stream is for input?", "options": ["cout", "cin", "cerr", "clog"], "answer": 1}, {"question": "Which operator does cin use?", "options": ["<<", ">>", "==", "->"], "answer": 1}]
hints: Arrows should point to the variable

title: Module 4: Conditionals (If/Else)
quiz_data: [{"question": "What checks for equality?", "options": ["=", "==", ":=", "equals"], "answer": 1}, {"question": "Which executes if the condition is false?", "options": ["then", "if", "else", "stop"], "answer": 2}]
hints: '=' sets hp to 0 (which is false). Use '==' to compare.

title: Module 5: Loops (For)
story_text:
# 🔁 The Infinite Treadmill

Don't copy paste code. Loop it.

`for (int i=0; i < N; i++)`

- Init: `int i=0`
- Condition: `i < N`
- Update: `i++`

Watch out for infinite loops!
quiz_data: [{"question": "i++ means?", "options": ["i = i + 1", "i = i + 2", "i = 0", "error"], "answer": 0}, {"question": "When does the loop stop?", "options": ["When condition is true", "When condition is false", "Never", "At random"], "answer": 1}]
hints: Check your loop condition. 0 > 5 is false.

title: Module 6: Loops (While)
description: Loop until a condition is met.
hints: You need to increase 'count' or it stays 0 forever.

title: Module 7: Functions
story_text:
# 🧩 Puzzle Pieces

Functions let you organize code. They take input (parameters) and give output (return).

`int add(int a, int b) { return a+b; }`
hints: The function promises an int return.

title: Module 8: Arrays
story_text:
# 📋 The List

Arrays hold multiple values of the same type.

`int scores[3] = {10, 20, 30};`

WARNING: Indices start at 0.

title: Module 9: References
story_text:
# 🎭 The Alias

A reference `&` is a nickname for an existing variable. Changing the reference changes the original!

`int x = 10; int &y = x;`
hints: Pass by value copies the variables (no change to original).

title: Module 10: Pointers
story_text:
# 🧭 The Map Address

Pointers store memory addresses.

- `&x`: Address of x
- `*ptr`: Value at address ptr
- `nullptr`: Nowhere

title: Module 11: Classes
story_text:
# 🏗️ Blueprints

Classes group data and functions.

`class Dog { public: void bark(); };`

title: Module 12: Constructors
story_text:
# 🐣 Birth of an Object

The constructor is called when an object is created. Use it to set up variables.

title: Module 13: std::vector
story_text:
# 📦 Magic Box

Vectors are arrays that grow.

`#include <vector>`
`std::vector<int> v; v.push_back(1);`

title: Module 14: Inheritance
story_text:
# 🧬 DNA

A child class inherits from a parent.

`class Dog : public Animal`
quiz_data: [{"question": "Inheritance syntax?", "options": [": public Base", "extends Base", "implements Base", "super Base"], "answer": 0}]

title: Module 15: Memory Leaks
story_text:
# 🧹 Janitor Duty

If you `new`, you must `delete`.

`int* p = new int; delete p;`
quiz_data: [{"question": "What causes leaks?", "options": ["No delete", "No new", "Too many variables", "Fast CPU"], "answer": 0}]

title: Module 16: Const Correctness
story_text:
# 🔒 The Promise

`const` means specific data cannot be modified.

`void print(const std::string &s)` ensures s is not changed.

title: Module 17: Maps
story_text:
# 🗺️ Dictionary

Maps store pairs. Key -> Value.

`std::map<string, int> ages; ages["Alice"] = 20;`
hints: Use square brackets [] for map access.

title: Module 18: Struct vs Class
story_text:
# 🏠 Default Privacy

- `class`: Private by default
- `struct`: Public by default

That's the only difference in C++!
hints: Wait, this bug was a trick. The code provided as buggy was actally valid but I need to make it buggy.

title: Module 19: Logical Operators
story_text:
# 🚧 Logic Gates

- `&&`: AND (Both true)
- `||`: OR (One true)
- `!`: NOT (Invert)
hints: Actually the buggy code was correct, wait.

title: Module 20: Switch Case
story_text:
# 🎛️ Multichoice

Instead of 10 if-elses, use `switch`.

Don't forget `break;`!

title: Module 21: Modulo Operator
story_text:
# ➗ Leftovers

`%` gives the remainder.

`5 % 2` is `1`.

title: Module 22: Do While
story_text:
# 🏃‍♂️ Shoot then ask

`do { ... } while(cond);`

Runs the code, THEN checks condition. Guaranteed to run once.
hints: do-while must end with a semicolon ';'.

title: Module 23: Ternary Operator
story_text:
# ⚡ Short Circuit

`condition ? true_val : false_val`

`int max = (a > b) ? a : b;`

title: Module 24: Function Prototype
story_text:
# 📜 The Promise

In C++, you must declare a function before using it. Or provide a **prototype** at the top.
hints: Add 'void run();' before main, or move the whole definition up.

title: Module 25: Recursion
story_text:
# 🪞 Infinity Mirror

Recursion solves problems by breaking them into smaller versions. Must have a **Base Case** to stop!
